title: What if everyone jumped at once?

A_identity.core_topic: Consequences of all humans gathering in one place and jumping together
A_identity.audience_inferred: Curious general viewers who like physics thought experiments and dry humour (inferred from text only)
A_identity.primary_question: What happens if everyone on Earth jumps at the same instant?
A_identity.promise: The physics has been covered before, but this telling gives the part others leave out.
A_identity.style: Deadpan present-tense narration with precise numbers and understated jokes
A_identity.pov: First-person narrator who places himself and the viewer inside the crowd ('we')

B_hook.opening_quote: This question comes from Thomas and many other people, who all asked
B_hook.construction: Reader question stated in full, social proof that it is popular, acknowledgement of earlier answers, then a pivot promising an untold part.
B_hook.first_curiosity_trigger: The claim that existing answers leave something out.
B_hook.conflict_or_contradiction: Others answered the physics correctly, yet the answer is said to be incomplete.
B_hook.withheld: What the 'whole story' is; the real consequence is logistics, not physics.
B_hook.audience_expectation: A physics answer about the Earth moving; the script plans to subvert it.
B_hook.promise_strength_reason: A clear, specific gap is opened in one short sentence and is fully paid later.
B_hook.opening_to_payoff: The tease is paid when the story shifts from the harmless jump to getting everyone home and the collapse that follows.
B_hook.why_may_hold: Viewers who already know the 'nothing happens' answer plausibly stay to learn what else there is.
B_hook.weaknesses: Two sentences naming prior blog coverage delay the first concrete image.

C_opening_beats.quote: What would happen if everyone on earth stood as close to each other as they could, jumped, and landed on the ground all at the same instant?
C_opening_beats.info_introduced: The full premise, attributed to a reader.

C_opening_beats.quote: This is one of the most popular questions submitted to What If.
C_opening_beats.info_introduced: Social proof and that it has been examined before.
C_opening_beats.question_active: If it is already answered, why this video?

C_opening_beats.quote: However, they don’t tell the whole story.
This crowd takes up an area the size of Rhode Island.
C_opening_beats.info_introduced: Magic transport assumption and a concrete location and scale.
C_opening_beats.question_active: What happens when they jump there?
C_opening_beats.unresolved: Both the jump result and the missing story.

stages.quote: However, they don’t tell the whole story.
stages.summary: Question stated and a gap opened beyond the known physics answer.
stages.link_to_next: Therefore the scenario must be set up concretely.

stages.quote: At the stroke of noon, everyone jumps.
stages.summary: Everyone is placed in Rhode Island and jumps.
stages.link_to_next: But the jump does almost nothing.

stages.quote: Earth outweighs us by a factor of over ten trillion.
stages.summary: Mass ratio, jump height and spread-out energy explain the non-event.
stages.link_to_next: Therefore the scene falls silent and attention turns to the people.

stages.quote: There are a lot of uncomfortable glances. Someone coughs.
stages.summary: An awkward pause, then phones fail and the abandoned world is shown.

stages.quote: how do we get everyone home?
they could run at 500% capacity for a hundred years without making a dent in the crowd
stages.summary: Airport, rail, ships and cars are each ruled out; shortages of food, water and sanitation follow.

stages.quote: Within weeks, Rhode Island is a graveyard of billions
stages.summary: The hidden consequence is the collapse of civilisation.
stages.link_to_next: But the original physics answer is restated as if it mattered most.

stages.quote: Note to future civilizations: let’s not try that again.
stages.summary: Orbit unaffected; a dry one-line warning.

D_spine.inciting_question: What would happen if everyone jumped at once?
D_spine.central_problem: The jump is harmless; having all humans in one place is not.
turning_points: The jump is declared a non-event
D_spine.climax: Rhode Island becomes a graveyard of billions.
D_spine.resolution: Survivors rebuild; the Earth's rotation and orbit are unchanged.

F_mechanics.quote: However, they don’t tell the whole story.
F_mechanics.construction: Concede the known answer, then claim it is incomplete.
F_mechanics.function: Turns an already-answered question into an open one.
F_mechanics.possible_audience_response: May make viewers who know the standard answer stay.
F_mechanics.reuse: Credit the common answer first, then state in one line that it misses something.

F_mechanics.quote: the Earth would still only be pushed down by less than an atom’s width
F_mechanics.construction: Best-case assumptions followed by a tiny, graspable unit.
F_mechanics.possible_audience_response: Plausibly a small surprise at how little happens.
F_mechanics.reuse: Grant every favourable assumption, then give the result in an everyday-or-atomic unit.

F_mechanics.quote: There are a lot of uncomfortable glances. Someone coughs.
F_mechanics.construction: Very short sentences after long ones, describing social awkwardness at planetary scale.
F_mechanics.function: Marks the pivot from physics to people.
F_mechanics.possible_audience_response: May get a laugh and reset attention.
F_mechanics.reuse: After a big anticlimax, cut to small human reactions in clipped sentences.

F_mechanics.quote: soccer balls complete their trajectories into now-vacant goals
F_mechanics.construction: A list of mundane objects continuing without people.
F_mechanics.function: Shows the consequence of the premise's assumption rather than stating it.
F_mechanics.reuse: Show a hidden side effect through three to five ordinary objects.

F_mechanics.quote: they could run at 500% capacity for a hundred years without making a dent in the crowd
F_mechanics.construction: Generous multiplier and long duration, still failing.
F_mechanics.function: Rules out the obvious solution with one figure.
F_mechanics.reuse: Give the solution an absurd advantage and show it still fails.

F_mechanics.quote: After all, who can stop you? All the cops are in Rhode Island.
F_mechanics.construction: Rhetorical question answered by the premise's own logic.
F_mechanics.function: Comic relief before the darkest section.
F_mechanics.reuse: Apply the premise literally to a small everyday rule.

F_mechanics.quote: the Earth’s rotation and orbit are completely unaffected
F_mechanics.construction: Restates the original trivial answer after the catastrophe, framed as most important.
F_mechanics.function: Ironic return to the opening question.
F_mechanics.reuse: End by answering the literal question as if the disaster were a side note.

J_ending.closing_quote: Note to future civilizations: let’s not try that again.
J_ending.final_insight: The physical question is trivial; the premise's hidden assumption is what kills everyone.
J_ending.earned_reason: The ironic restatement only works because the catastrophe has been built step by step.

strengths: Answers the literal question early, then opens a larger one.
Uses concrete local detail (named airport, highways) to make an absurd premise feel real.
Ending returns to the opening question with reversed weight.
improvements: The prior-coverage sentences could be shortened to reach the tease sooner.
Transport failures could be compressed to avoid repeating the same verdict.
K_assessment.distinctive_technique: Treating the setup assumption (everyone in one place) as the real disaster.
K_assessment.biggest_risk: Viewers wanting only the physics answer get it early and may plausibly leave.
K_assessment.lesson: When the obvious answer is 'nothing happens', follow the consequences of the question's assumptions instead.

L_formula: State the reader's question in full and note how often it is asked.
Credit existing answers, then say they leave something out.
Fix the scenario in one concrete place.
Give the literal physics answer quickly with one scale comparison.
Pause on small human reactions, then show what the assumption broke elsewhere.
Pose the practical follow-up question and rule out each solution with numbers.
Let the consequences reach their bleak end.
Restate the literal answer as if it were the main point and close with a dry warning.

lenses.architect: Two-part build: a short answered question followed by a longer consequence timeline it was hiding.
lenses.surgeon: The pivot is carried by three very short sentences in a row, which separate the physics half from the logistics half.
lenses.viral: The cops line is the most quotable: a rhetorical question answered by the premise itself in seven words.
lenses.critic: The spoken aside about airport bathrooms is unscripted-sounding and sits oddly inside a scripted scenario.
lenses.curiosity: The script answers its title question early and survives on a second gap opened before the first is closed.
lenses.platform: The opening restates the title question in natural search wording; the phone-silence passage plausibly stands alone as a short.
lenses.integrator: Physics, logistics and dark comedy are joined by a single location that every section returns to.
lenses.tradeoffs: Early answer gives honesty and trust but spends the title's curiosity in the first third.
